name: Dropbox
foundedNote: The S-1 states it plainly: "We were incorporated in May 2007 as Evenflow, Inc., a Delaware corporation, and changed our name to Dropbox, Inc. in October 2009." The 2009 Form D filed under the Evenflow name independently gives jurisdiction Delaware and year of incorporation 2007. No source fixes the day — Delaware's registry is captcha-gated and the S-1 gives only the month — so this is dated to the month rather than inventing a date. There is no earlier partnership: Drew Houston conceived Dropbox in early 2007, applied to Y Combinator alone in April 2007, and recruited Arash Ferdowsi as co-founder before the Summer 2007 batch, so the Delaware incorporation is the earliest formal founding.

regressions.note: This checks agreement with companiesmarketcap, NOT ground truth. The hand-derived figure is $6.98B (FY2025 10-K: 167.2M Class A + 75.7M Class B + 8.3M co-founder RSAs = 251.2M x the $27.80 close). The pipeline computes $7.26B and companiesmarketcap publishes $7.32B — both ~4-5% high, because Dropbox retired roughly 18% of its stock during 2025 and both methods lag a share count moving that fast. Dropbox exposes no cover-page share tag to the SEC companyfacts API, so the series runs on weighted-average basic shares and cannot reach the hand-derived number. The regression guards against a future tag or split regression; it does not certify the level.

public.sharesNote: No dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding and no us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding: Dropbox tags its cover count with a share-class axis, which companyfacts does not expose. Falls back to weighted-average basic shares, so every quarterly point is marked soft.

events.note: Below the inclusion floor: an accelerator batch investment, not a round led by a named venture firm. Recorded but never plotted. The amount is left null on purpose — Y Combinator's standard Summer 2007 cheque is widely repeated as $15,000-$20,000 for 5-7%, but no filing, YC post or company statement I could load states Dropbox's figure, and the 2009 Form D lumps every pre-2009 sale into one $7,252,763 offering. Dated to the start of the Summer 2007 batch; no source fixes the day.

events.nameConflict: Usually called the seed round. The charter letter is almost certainly A-1, which sits below Series A in price — the opposite of the usual ordering, because it is a note converting at a discount rather than a later round.
events.note: The first money from a named venture firm, so it clears the inclusion floor even though it is a note rather than a priced round. TechCrunch reports $1.2M of convertible debt from Sequoia Capital with Amidzad Partners. The date is the "date of first sale" on the Form D that Evenflow, Inc. filed in 2009 (2007-09-24); that Form D covers a single $7,252,763 offering of both equity and debt to 8 investors, i.e. this note plus the 2008 Series A together, which is exactly the "$7.2 million raised prior" TechCrunch cites in 2011. No valuation was ever disclosed and a note has no post-money by construction, so this is recorded, not plotted. The S-1 cap table's Series A-1 (51.9M shares post-split, $1.3M aggregate liquidation preference, ~$0.025/share against Series A's ~$0.094) is almost certainly this note converted with its discount — an inference from the arithmetic, not a statement in the filing.

Drew Houston corrected the record himself to TechCrunch in 2009: "$6 million, and it was back in October 2008," led by Sequoia, with Accel participating (GigaOm had reported $7.25M in summer 2009 — that figure is the 2009 Form D's cumulative $7,252,763, which also includes the 2007 note). The S-1 cap table corroborates the size exactly: Series A carries a $6.0M aggregate liquidation preference at $0.09/share post-split ($0.06 pre-split). No post-money was ever disclosed and the S-1 gives no 2008 share count to reconstruct one, so valuation stays null and the round is not plotted. Aggregators circulate a $25M post-money with no primary attribution; it is not used here.

New investors Benchmark, Goldman Sachs, Greylock, IVP, RIT Capital Partners and Valiant Capital; Sequoia, Accel and Hadi and Ali Partovi followed on. TechCrunch reported the $4B mark when the round was still being assembled in August 2011 and again on close, and Forbes restated it independently in 2014, so the figure is treated as confirmed — though no source says whether it is pre- or post-money, hence basis "unspecified". TechCrunch also notes this took Dropbox's lifetime raise to $257.2M, which reconciles to $1.2M + $6M + $250M. The S-1 cap table shows Series B at $13.58/share post-split ($9.05 pre-split) with a $264.8M aggregate liquidation preference — $14.8M more than the announced $250M, implying a later tranche the press never covered; the announced round size is used for the event.

The amount is the S-1's exact figure: 18,460,901 shares of Series C sold to 55 accredited investors at ~$19.1012/share ($28.6518 post-split) for $352,625,362, from January through April 2014. The date is the Form D's date of first sale. The press numbers were all partial views of that: WSJ (via TechCrunch, 2014-01-17) reported ~$250M at $10B; the Form D filed 2014-02-24 showed a $450M offering with $324,999,850 sold so far, which is where Forbes's "$450 million" came from. Valuation is soft because well-sourced figures disagree — WSJ and every outlet following it say $10B, while Forbes, working from the Delaware restated certificate via VC Experts, computes ~$9.6B on ~502M fully diluted shares at the $19.1012 issue price. The higher figure is used, per policy, with the rejected $9.6B recorded here.

events.lead: Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Deutsche Bank (joint book-runners)
events.note: A visible down round at the IPO: Dropbox priced at $8.23B against the $10B private mark of 2014, four years earlier. Both inputs come from the final prospectus — $21.00 per share and 391,903,011 shares of Class A and Class B outstanding after the offering and the concurrent private placement. That count excludes the 14,733,333 Class A shares under the co-founders' unvested restricted stock awards; including them the figure is $8.54B, still below $10B. The company sold 26,822,409 shares for $563.3M gross, selling stockholders another 9,177,591 (the $756.0M total usually quoted), and Salesforce Ventures bought $100.0M more in a concurrent private placement. The stock then closed its first day at $29.89, up 42%, which is ~$11.71B — the public series picks the market up from there.

curatorNotes: Dropbox has no usable cover-page share tag, so every quarterly point in the public series is computed from a weighted average and is correctly drawn hollow. dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding and us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding are both absent from its XBRL facts — it is a Class A/Class B filer and tags the cover count with a share-class axis the companyfacts API does not expose — and us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued carries only two non-dimensional values (2020 and 2021). The cascade lands on us-gaap:WeightedAverageNumberOfSharesOutstandingBasic, which holds 22 rows. Two structural gaps follow. First, there is no Q4 row at all: the 10-K reports a full-year weighted average, which the >100-day span filter correctly drops, so every 31 December point is priced on the Q3 average, roughly 85 days stale. Second, Dropbox's 2018 and 2019 10-Qs tagged the figure as WeightedAverageNumberOfShareOutstandingBasicAndDiluted, so the Basic series only begins with the 2019 periods carried as comparatives in the 2020 10-Qs; the six quarters from 2018-06-30 to 2019-09-30 have no share row within 200 days and drop out, leaving 2018 covered only by companiesmarketcap's annual point and by the IPO event itself. The cross-check still passes comfortably: seven overlapping years, worst 2.69% (2024), and 0.28-1.45% everywhere else. What that agreement hides is that companiesmarketcap carries the same lag. Hand-derived truth at 2025-12-31, from the FY2025 10-K, is 167.2M Class A plus 75.7M Class B issued and outstanding plus the 8.3M legally outstanding but unvested co-founder restricted stock awards the balance sheet excludes and the cover page includes — 251.2M shares at the $27.80 close, or $6.98B. The pipeline's 261.1M Q3 average gives $7.26B (3.9% high) and companiesmarketcap gives $7.32B (4.9% high). Dropbox retired about 18% of its stock during 2025, so a one-quarter-stale count costs several per cent there while costing well under one per cent in the flatter years. Excluded events: the March 2017 $600M revolving credit facility is debt, not equity; the third-party tender offer that ran somewhere between 2014 and 2017 (8,193,202 Class A shares issued on conversion, per the S-1) has no disclosed price or date and cannot be turned into a valuation.
unresolved: The exact day of the May 2007 Delaware incorporation. The S-1 gives only the month and Delaware's registry is captcha-gated.

Y Combinator's Summer 2007 investment amount and the equity it bought. Every figure in circulation ($15,000-$20,000, 5-7%) traces to secondary retellings, and the 2009 Form D reports only the $7,252,763 cumulative total.
The 2008 Series A post-money. Never disclosed, and the S-1 gives no 2008 share count from which to reconstruct it.
Whether the $4B (2011) and $10B (2014) marks are pre- or post-money. No source says.
Whether Series A-1 really is the converted 2007 Sequoia note. The arithmetic ($1.3M aggregate at a third of the Series A price) fits, but no filing says so.
The date and price of the 2014-2017 third-party tender offer disclosed in the S-1.
